Known science foundations of Interstellar Navigation Through Sparse Data.

AutoNav demonstrated autonomous asteroid tracking on Deep Space 1. New Horizons used optical navigation to hit its Pluto and Arrokoth targets. Pulsar-based navigation (XNAV) is tested on the ISS via NICER/SEXTANT. Star trackers are standard. Interstellar cruise adds years of no-contact operation and relativistic corrections.

Physical and engineering constraints on Interstellar Navigation Through Sparse Data.

No GPS, no ground updates, no rescue for years at a time. Onboard clocks drift; pulsars and stars are the references. A navigation error at 0.2c is uncorrectable after the fact.

Scale analysis across 3 quantities spans 19.7 orders of magnitude; the dominant scale separation is one-way light time at 100 AU vs pulsar timing stability at 19.7 orders of magnitude (one-way light time at 100 AU larger). Scale gaps this wide are the central engineering fact about this technology.
